data.exact_reserve_text: The claims incurred, as stated within the financial statements of GBP 5.5m (2013: GBP 4.2m) includes a deterioration of GBP 0.3m on 2012 & prior years and a marginal movement on the other years of account (2013: GBP 1.4m deterioration) in relation to claims incurred at the prior year end. The unfavourable development on the 2012 & prior years follows adverse experience in relation to the Syndicate's long-tailed legacy portfolio.

prior_year_events.event_name: Adverse claims development on long-tailed legacy portfolio
prior_year_events.impact_description: Adverse development on 2011 & prior years led to deterioration incorporated into the 2012 closure and contributed to the loss at 36 months.

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2014 the Syndicate's gross claims outstanding balance was GBP 17.603m. During 2014 there was a small adverse prior-year development (deterioration) of approximately GBP 0.3m (net) attributable to the Syndicate's longtailed legacy termlife book (noted as affecting 2012 & prior / 2011 & prior). The movement reflects adverse claims experience in the legacy portfolio; the report does not disclose a gross prioryear movement explicitly, so the quantified GBP 0.3m is reported on a net basis.
raw_causal_phrases: deterioration of GBP 0.3m on 2012 & prior years
marginal movement on the other years of account (2013: GBP 1.4m deterioration)
The unfavourable development on the 2012 & prior years follows adverse experience in relation to the Syndicate's long-tailed legacy portfolio
data.data_quality_notes: No explicit GROSS prior-year movement for claims outstanding was presented. The note states a deterioration of GBP 0.3m on 2012 & prior years in the context of 'claims incurred' (a net/after-reinsurance P&L line). The gross claims outstanding opening balance is taken from the Balance Sheet (explicit). Prior year development is therefore reported on a net basis (fallback) because no gross prior-year movement figure was identified in the technical reserves reconciliation or a gross claims development triangle.
